newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK--No new data, focus on FOMC. [CORRECTED 00:16 GMT]
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK--No new data, focus on FOMC. [CORRECTED 00:16 GMT]

text.p: With no new economic data brought to its plate on Friday, the U.S. Treasury market will continue to debate the prospective outcome of next week's Federal Reserve monetary policy meeting, analysts said.

"A lot of people are running analyses and stories based on past commentary from Fed officials, trying to figure out who's going to vote which way (on whether to raise interest rates)," said Waldo Best, senior economist at BZW Securities, (corrects company name from BZT Securities).
"Some of the stories say the presidential election is not a factor and that anyone who says it is, is not really a Fed watcher."
At various times, some commentators have said the Fed would rather not raise interest rates in the middle of the presidential election season.
The U.S. Treasury market retreated on Thursday after several unexpectedly firm economic reports joined forces with some bearish technical factors.

A surprising gain in August housing starts to an annualized 1.525 million from an annualized 1.46 million in July perturbed a market that had expected higher mortgage rates to curb growth in the housing sector of the economy.
Elliott Platt, managing director, economic research at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette, said the outcome of the FOMC meeting is a close call.
Platt expects economic growth to slow to below two percent in the second half of the year. But he also thinks the Fed will raise rates by 25 basis points at its Tuesday meeting.
"It boils down to their perception of (the balance between) risk (and) reward," Platt said.
Platt said the Fed will be more concerned about the risk of not tightening when it was necessary than the risks of undertaking a tightening that proves to be unnecessary.
